head: fc6da0469227fc263c03bf9ec54cc0fc43eb857d
headline: Customers can now download their own invoices as a spreadsheet file. The code looks safe, but its test has never been run.
what_changed: Signed-in customers get a new download at a new web address. It gives them a spreadsheet file (CSV) of their own invoices for their accountant.
The file lists invoice number, date, total and status, newest first.
Totals show as normal money amounts like 123.45 instead of cents. The existing invoice list still uses cents.
The download is protected against a known spreadsheet trick: values that would run as formulas get a leading apostrophe, so they show as plain text instead.
One automated test was added, plus a small settings file so tests can find the app. The code is not yet committed, pushed or opened for review, because Python isn't installed on the machine.

risks.title: The new test has never actually been run
risks.explanation: Python wasn't available on the machine, so nobody has confirmed the test passes. When I read the code it looks correct, but a small mistake could still show up on the first run. Have a developer run the tests before this is published.

risks.title: Some invoice numbers may get an extra apostrophe
risks.explanation: An invoice number or status starting with a symbol such as =, +, - or @ gets a leading apostrophe in the file. This blocks a known spreadsheet attack. But if your real invoice numbers ever start with '-' or '+', accountants will see the apostrophe. This doesn't matter if your numbers look like 'INV-001'.

questions_for_developer: Can you install Python, run the full test suite, and confirm the new invoice download test passes before we publish?
Do any of our real invoice numbers start with a symbol like '-' or '+'? If so, they will show a leading apostrophe in the downloaded spreadsheet. Is that acceptable?
Does the website have a 'Download CSV' button that links to the new address, or does that still need building?
good_news: The download uses the existing sign-in check and only fetches invoices belonging to the signed-in customer. The test checks that another customer's invoice is left out.
The change is small and self-contained. The existing invoice list works the same and now uses the same lookup as the download.
The browser is told not to keep a saved copy of the file, which helps on shared computers.
